_note: Real lessons from the Maryland state standards, not invented ones. Every `objective` is the source document's own wording and every `standard` is a genuine code from that document -- do not edit either to make a lesson sound better, and do not invent codes for new lessons. The source PDFs are listed below.
_sources: Maryland College and Career Ready Standards in English Language Arts, State Board attachment 2025/0729
Maryland College and Career Ready Standards for Mathematics, State Board attachment 2025/0729 (PreK-8)
Next Generation Science Standards, adopted 2013 as the Maryland Science Standards
_provenance: Fetched, parsed and cited in the EduSystems project (Aug 2026); the PDFs live in that repo under docs/reference/. Carried across rather than re-scraped so the citations stay the verified ones.

_concepts_note: Concepts are COMPONENTS of their lesson's standard, and each one cites that same real code rather than a code of its own. Inventing a plausible-looking identifier for a sub-skill would be a fabricated citation, which is worse than no citation at all -- see the header of scripts/data/curriculum.gd. 'at' is how many times that lesson must have been taught before the concept is unlocked.
_difficulty_note: 1 to 5. It scales how long the work takes and how often a child gets stuck on it, so a hard lesson is genuinely harder to get a class through -- and it is shown on the curriculum page, because a difficulty you cannot see before you commit is a trap rather than a choice.
